original_question: Is every orbit equivalence relation arising from a Borel action of a countable amenable group hyperfinite?
target_in_paper: Section 11 (Jing Yu), Problem 40 (Weiss’ question): "Is the orbit equivalence relation of Borel action of countable amenable group hyperfinite?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem in the paper: it asks about orbit equivalence relations coming from Borel actions of countable amenable groups and whether they are hyperfinite. So the mathematical target is essentially correct and very close to the paper’s official wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The ambient space on which the group acts should be made explicit: a standard Borel space X.
The universal quantifiers should be written out explicitly: for every countable amenable group G and every Borel action G ↷ X.
The induced orbit equivalence relation should be defined explicitly, e.g. x E_G^X y iff there exists g in G with g·x = y.
To make the question stand-alone, "hyperfinite" should be unpacked as: E_G^X is an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations on X.

It is worth making explicit that Problem 40 does not assume the action is free, measure preserving, ergodic, or probability-measure preserving; it is stated for Borel actions in general. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: For every countable amenable group G and every Borel action G ↷ X on a standard Borel space X, is the induced orbit equivalence relation E_G^X on X, defined by x E_G^X y iff there exists g in G such that g·x = y, hyperfinite; that is, can E_G^X be written as an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations?
justification: The paper states this as Problem 40 in Section 11 under Jing Yu, naming it Weiss’ question. The immediately following context lists specific classes of groups for which hyperfiniteness of orbit equivalence relations is already known, which confirms that your draft is targeting this exact amenable-group problem rather than a broader neighboring question. The adjacent Problem 41 then turns to graph-growth variants, so the refined version should stay with the original group-action formulation and not drift into the nearby graph setting. The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 40, so no alternate formulation from the paper should be supplied. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
